mainTopic: How בשר בחלב is shown to be אסור בהנאה, the rules of כלאי הכרם, and healing with forbidden things
overview: The amud continues the proof that בשר בחלב is אסור בהנאה. The proof goes through a chain of cases: ערלה, then חמץ בפסח, then כלאי הכרם. Each case covers the weakness of the one before it. The גמרא then asks whether אביי's rule breaks the proof. His rule is that one gets מלקות for כלאי הכרם even for unusual benefit. The answer is no, because the verse about בשר בחלב also does not say 'eating.' The challenger disagrees and learns from נבילה that only normal benefit is punished. Next, רבי אדא בר אהבה learns that even the original seeds of כלאי הכרם become forbidden. רבא reconciles this with a משנה about a pot with a hole: a plant sown in the vineyard is forbidden once it takes root, while a plant brought in later is forbidden only if it grows there. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that one may heal with any forbidden thing except עבודה זרה, even in danger, based on ״בכל נפשך״. רבין's broader version of this rule begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ערלה cannot be the model because it was never permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning בשר בחלב from ערלה, because ערלה never had a time when it was permitted, while meat and milk each did.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare to ערלה? ערלה never had a time when it was permitted. Can you say the same about בשר בחלב, which did have a time when it was permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is rejecting the proof from ערלה. It points out that ערלה is stricter in a way that בשר בחלב is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה fruit is forbidden from the moment it grows, so it never had a 'kosher moment.' Meat and milk were each permitted before being cooked together. Maybe a food forbidden from the start is more likely to be אסור בהנאה, so ערלה cannot teach us about בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden to eat and to benefit from
A time when the item was fit and permitted
Meat cooked with milk
'What about...?' The standard opening for showing that a comparison does not work

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying ערלה is permitted in benefit. ערלה is definitely אסור בהנאה. The point is only that ערלה has an extra strictness, so it cannot serve as a model for בשר בחלב.

phrases.english: What [comparison can be made] to orlah,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
phrases.english: as it never had a time when it was fit?
Will you say [the same] about meat in milk,
which had a time when it was fit!
phrases.notes: Meat alone and milk alone were permitted before being cooked together.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְעׇרְלָה שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proposed derivation of בשר בחלב from ערלה, which came earlier.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects ערלה as a source for the הנאה prohibition of בשר בחלב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ערלה has a stricter feature (no שעת הכושר) that בשר בחלב lacks.

steps.title: חמץ בפסח proves that a prior permitted time does not matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings חמץ בפסח as a new model: it was permitted before פסח, and it is still אסור בהנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let חמץ בפסח prove the point. It had a time when it was permitted, and still it is forbidden to benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection to ערלה by bringing a different example that also had a permitted time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ was fine before פסח, yet it is אסור בהנאה during פסח. This shows that having a שעת הכושר does not stop something from being אסור בהנאה. So the objection from Step 1 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Leavened bread during פסח
'Will prove.' Brings a case that disproves the objection
Forbidden to derive any benefit from

phrases.english: Let leavened bread on Passover prove,
as it had a time when it was fit,
and [yet] it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of Step 1 with a new model case.
steps.raayaObject: That בשר בחלב can be אסור בהנאה even though it once had a permitted time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: חמץ בפסח, which was permitted before פסח and is still אסור בהנאה.

steps.title: חמץ cannot be the model because it carries כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects חמץ as a model, because eating חמץ is punished with כרת and eating בשר בחלב is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare to חמץ בפסח? Eating it is punished with כרת. Can you say the same about בשר בחלב, which is not punished with כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a new weakness: חמץ is a more serious prohibition than בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe חמץ is אסור בהנאה because it is so severe that it carries כרת. בשר בחלב only carries מלקות, so the comparison may not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Punished with כרת, spiritual cutting off, the severe divine penalty

phrases.english: What [comparison can be made] to leavened bread on Passover,
as it is punished with karet?
Will you say [the same] about meat in milk,
which is not punished with karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח שֶׁכֵּן עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the model case brought in Step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects חמץ בפסח as a source for בשר בחלב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חמץ carries כרת, a severity that בשר בחלב lacks.

steps.title: כלאי הכרם proves that כרת is not needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings כלאי הכרם: it has no כרת, yet it is אסור בהנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let כלאי הכרם prove the point. There is no כרת for it, and still it is forbidden to benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the כרת objection by bringing a prohibition without כרת that is still אסור בהנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלאי הכרם shows that a prohibition does not need כרת to be אסור בהנאה. Together, the examples cover each other's weaknesses, so בשר בחלב can be learned as אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures of grain or vegetables planted in a vineyard
'Will prove' (plural form, matching כלאי)

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the derivation that בשר בחלב is אסור בהנאה, and it sets up the next question about whether אביי's teaching on כלאי הכרם breaks the proof.

phrases.english: Let diverse kinds in a vineyard prove,
as one is not punished with karet,
and [yet] it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of Step 3 with a final model case.
steps.raayaObject: That בשר בחלב can be אסור בהנאה even without כרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: כלאי הכרם, which has no כרת and is still אסור בהנאה.

steps.title: If אביי is right, כלאי הכרם should be too strict to compare
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if one gets מלקות for כלאי הכרם even for unusual benefit, then כלאי הכרם is stricter and should not be a model for בשר בחלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If אביי's teaching is true, we should be able to refute the proof: how can you compare to כלאי הכרם, where one gets מלקות even for benefiting in an unusual way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to אביי's earlier teaching and uses it to attack the last proof. If כלאי הכרם has an extra strictness, the comparison should break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that one gets מלקות for כלאי הכרם even for benefit שלא כדרך הנאתן. That would make כלאי הכרם stricter than בשר בחלב, and the whole chain of proofs could fall. Since the גמרא did not raise this refutation, maybe אביי's teaching is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if it is so.' Tests a teaching by following where it leads
'Let us refute.' We should be able to raise a refutation
They give מלקות (lashes)
Not in the normal way of benefiting from them

phrases.english: And if it is so [as Abaye says], let us refute:
phrases.notes: Refers back to אביי's teaching on כלאי הכרם earlier.

phrases.english: What [comparison can be made] to diverse kinds in a vineyard,
as one is flogged for them
even [when benefiting] not in their usual manner of benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the final proof of Step 4 to challenge אביי's earlier teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's teaching that one gets מלקות for כלאי הכרם even for unusual benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כלאי הכרם were that strict, the derivation of בשר בחלב from it should have been refuted. Since the גמרא accepts the derivation without that refutation, אביי's teaching seems wrong.

steps.title: בשר בחלב also lacks the word eating, so the strictness applies to it too
steps.stepSummary: אביי's defense: the refutation cannot even be finished, because בשר בחלב also has no word 'eating' in its verse, so it shares the same strictness as כלאי הכרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי would answer: 'Will you say...' about what? Will you say that for בשר בחלב one gets מלקות only for benefit in the normal way? Is the word 'eating' written about בשר בחלב?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by showing that the refutation cannot be completed. There is no real difference between the two prohibitions on this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every refutation needs a second half: 'but בשר בחלב is not like that.' Here that half fails. אביי's reason for כלאי הכרם is that the verse does not say 'eating,' and the verse about בשר בחלב ('לא תבשל', do not cook) does not say 'eating' either. So both get מלקות even for unusual benefit, and the proof from כלאי הכרם stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In what?' About what point?
Its normal way of benefit
'Is it as if...?' Introduces a rhetorical question expecting 'no'
'Is eating written in it?' Does the verse use the word 'eating'?

steps.whatToRemember: בשר בחלב is learned to be אסור בהנאה through ערלה, then חמץ, then כלאי הכרם. אביי's rule (מלקות even שלא כדרך הנאתן, because 'eating' is not written) does not break the proof, because בשר בחלב also has no word 'eating' and so shares that same rule.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'תאמר בבשר בחלב שאין לוקין עליו אלא דרך הנאתו' is not a ruling. It is the refutation's needed second half, quoted only so that it can be rejected with 'אטו...'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the Torah's word choice ('eating' versus not 'eating') decides whether there are מלקות for unusual benefit. It also suggests that בשר בחלב shares this rule with כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: And Abaye [would say]: 'Will you say' about what?!
phrases.notes: Asks what the second half of the refutation could possibly be.

phrases.english: Will you say regarding meat in milk
that one is not flogged for it
except [for benefit] in its usual manner?
Is it as if regarding meat in milk
eating is written in it?!
phrases.notes: The verse says 'לא תבשל' (do not cook), not 'do not eat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5 and defends אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the refutation cannot be completed, because the two cases are the same on the relevant point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלאי הכרם is uniquely strict (מלקות even for unusual benefit), so it cannot be a model for בשר בחלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason for that strictness (the verse does not say 'eating') applies equally to בשר בחלב, so there is no refutation and אביי's teaching stands.

steps.title: What about the Sage who raised the objection?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the Sage who challenged אביי explains the missing word 'eating' in the verse about בשר בחלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage, the one who raised the objection, how does he deal with this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי has just said that בשר בחלב also has no word 'eating' in its verse. Now the גמרא asks how the Sage who challenged him would answer that point. This short question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's defense depends on reading the missing word 'eating' as a sign of strictness. The challenger must have some other way to read the verse. Otherwise his challenge from כלאי הכרם would have no force.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other Sage)
Raises an objection or challenge

phrases.english: And the other one, who raised this objection?
phrases.notes: How does he answer אביי's point?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the challenger answers אביי's point from Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the challenger explains the missing word 'eating' in the verse about בשר בחלב.

steps.title: The challenger learns from נבילה that only normal benefit brings מלקות
steps.stepSummary: The challenger holds that בשר בחלב is learned from נבילה precisely to teach that מלקות applies only for normal benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that this is exactly why he learns it from נבילה: just as with נבילה one is punished only for normal benefit, so too with בשר בחלב, only for normal benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7. The challenger says בשר בחלב is linked to נבילה, and נבילה's verse does say 'eating.' So בשר בחלב gets the same rule: punishment only for normal use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The missing word 'eating' does not make בשר בחלב strict, because the comparison to נבילה brings that word back in. So בשר בחלב is lenient here, and כלאי הכרם, which punishes even unusual benefit, stays stricter. That keeps the challenge from Step 5 alive.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Learns a law from another case
The normal way of using or benefiting from it
For this reason / for this purpose

steps.confusionAlert: ספריא notes that the correct source is really טריפה ('throw it to the dogs'), not נבילה. Either way, the point is the same: the source verse says 'eating,' so only normal benefit is punished.

phrases.english: He holds: for this reason he learns it from an animal carcass.
phrases.notes: Through the גזירה שוה of איסי בן יהודה.

phrases.english: Just as with an animal carcass, only its normal way of benefit is punished,
so too with meat in milk, only its normal way of benefit.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison to נבילה limits מלקות for בשר בחלב to normal benefit, so כלאי הכרם remains stricter.

steps.title: אביי reads the missing word 'eating' as a strictness
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds the Torah left out 'eating' for בשר בחלב on purpose, to teach that one gets מלקות even for unusual benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי holds: this is why the Torah did not write 'eating' in its own verse, to teach that one gets מלקות even for benefit that is not the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states אביי's side of the disagreement. The Torah left out the word 'eating' on purpose, to make בשר בחלב strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides look at the same missing word. The challenger says the link to נבילה limits the punishment. אביי says the missing word itself teaches strictness, which matches כלאי הכרם. So for אביי, the model still works.

keyTerms.meaning: In its own verse (the verse about the איסור itself)
We give מלקות (lashes)
Not in the normal way of benefit

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about one missing word. For the challenger, בשר בחלב is punished only for normal benefit (from נבילה). For אביי, it is punished even for unusual benefit, just like כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: And Abaye holds: for this reason it did not write
phrases.notes: The Torah intentionally left out the word.

phrases.english: 'eating' in its own verse,
to say that one gets lashes for it
even when the benefit is not in its normal way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי: לְהָכִי לֹא כָּתַב אֲכִילָה בְּגוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אביי's opposite reading, in contrast to Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The missing word 'eating' teaches strictness, so בשר בחלב matches כלאי הכרם.

steps.title: Why not reject כלאי הכרם because it never had a permitted time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why no one rejected the model by saying that כלאי הכרם was forbidden from the start and never had a permitted time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let one reject the proof this way: what about כלאי הכרם, which never had a time when it was permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a new way to reject the comparison. בשר בחלב was permitted before it was cooked, but כלאי הכרם seems to be forbidden from the moment it grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that was never permitted can more easily be אסור בהנאה. Something that once was permitted, like meat and milk, might be weaker. Since this obvious rejection was never raised, the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him reject (raise a פירכא against the comparison)
A time when it was fit and permitted
Mixed plantings in a vineyard, forbidden in benefit

phrases.english: But let him reject it: what about diverse kinds in a vineyard,
since it never had
a time when it was permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפְרוֹךְ: מָה לְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new possible weakness in the כלאי הכרם model from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of בשר בחלב to כלאי הכרם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כלאי הכרם was never permitted, but בשר בחלב was, so the two cases are not equal.

steps.title: The seeds of כלאי הכרם are forbidden too, so it did have a permitted time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אדא בר אהבה learns from the missing challenge that even the original seeds become forbidden, and they were permitted before they took root.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אדא בר אהבה said: This teaches that with כלאי הכרם, the original plants themselves become forbidden. They did have a permitted time, before they took root.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אדא בר אהבה explains why the challenge was not asked. The original seed or sapling also becomes forbidden, and it was fine before it rooted in the vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the new growth were forbidden, then כלאי הכרם truly never had a permitted time. But if the original seed is forbidden too, then it had a permitted time before rooting, just like meat and milk before cooking. So the comparison still works.

keyTerms.meaning: This proves / this teaches us
Their original part (the seed or sapling that was planted)
Taking root

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a practical ruling about כלאי הכרם: not only the new growth, but the original planted material also becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Adda bar Ahava said:
This teaches that with diverse kinds in a vineyard,
their original roots or seeds become forbidden,
since they had a time when they were permitted
before taking root.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by drawing a new rule from the fact that the challenge was not raised.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from silence that changes the facts of the model case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלאי הכרם is forbidden from its first growth and never had a permitted time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The original seeds also become forbidden, and they were permitted before they took root.

steps.title: רב שמעיה challenges from a משנה about a pot with a hole
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה brings a משנה that forbids the plant only if it grew one part in two hundred, which suggests only the new growth is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה challenged: One who carries a pot with a hole in it through a vineyard: if the plant grew by one two-hundredth, it is forbidden. If it grew, yes. If it did not grow, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה attacks רבי אדא בר אהבה's rule. The משנה forbids the plant only if it grew. That suggests the original plant is not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original plant became forbidden as soon as it took root, the משנה would not need any new growth. Since the משנה requires growth of one part in two hundred, it seems only the added growth is forbidden. That goes against Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a challenge from a source
A plant pot with a hole, which counts as connected to the ground
Two hundred (growth of one part in two hundred)
It grew / increased

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya raised an objection:
One who carries a perforated pot through a vineyard,
if it grew by one two-hundredth, it is forbidden.
If it grew, yes; if it did not grow, no!
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: without growth, nothing is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שְׁמַעְיָה: הַמַּעֲבִיר עָצִיץ נָקוּב בַּכֶּרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אדא בר אהבה's rule from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אדא בר אהבה's rule that the original plants of כלאי הכרם become forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids only when there is new growth, so the original plant itself must not be forbidden.

steps.title: Two words in the verse: planted from the start versus brought in later
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction between רבי אדא בר אהבה and the משנה. He shows that the פסוק describes two different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two expressions are written. It says 'the seed' and it says 'the fullness.' How do they fit together? If it was planted in the vineyard from the start, it becomes forbidden once it takes root. If it was planted elsewhere and brought in, then if it grew, yes, it is forbidden. If it did not grow, no, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב שמעיה's challenge from the משנה. He explains that each opinion is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״הַזָּרַע״ (the seed itself) teaches that the whole plant, original seed included, becomes forbidden once it takes root. ״הַמְּלֵאָה״ (the fullness, meaning growth) teaches that sometimes only growth makes it forbidden. רבא assigns the first to a plant sown in the vineyard and the second to a plant brought in later, for example in a pot with a hole. The משנה about growing one part in two hundred is talking about the second case.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses (expressions) are written
The seed, which implies the original seed itself is forbidden
The fullness, meaning the growth
Taking root
Planted elsewhere and then brought into the vineyard

steps.whatToRemember: Planted in the vineyard from the start: forbidden at הַשְׁרָשָׁה, seed and all. Brought in already growing: forbidden only if it grew there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי אדא בר אהבה's reading, which says the original seeds also become forbidden. The משנה is moved to a different case.

phrases.english: Rava said: Two verses (expressions) are written:
It is written 'the seed'
phrases.notes: This implies the seed itself is forbidden.

phrases.english: and it is written 'the fullness,'
phrases.notes: This implies only the growth is forbidden.

phrases.english: How is this reconciled?
If it was planted there from the start, it is forbidden upon taking root.
If it was planted elsewhere and brought in,
if it grew more, yes, it is forbidden,
if it did not grow, no, it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שמעיה's challenge from the משנה in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) based on two expressions in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's requirement of growth seemed to contradict the idea that the original seed becomes forbidden upon rooting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rooting forbids a plant sown in the vineyard. Growth is required only for a plant brought in from elsewhere.

steps.title: One may heal with anything except wood of an idolatrous tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן: healing with forbidden substances is allowed, except with עצי אשירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One may heal oneself with anything, except wood of an אשירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about benefit from forbidden things. It quotes רבי יוחנן's rule about healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule permits using forbidden items for healing. It makes one exception: wood from a tree worshipped as עבודה זרה. The rule does not yet say whether the person is in danger, and that gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: One may heal oneself
Wood of a tree worshipped as idolatry
Except for

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
One may heal oneself with anything,
except for wood of an asheira.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected by the general theme of benefit from forbidden things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All forbidden items may be used for healing except wood of an אשירה.

steps.title: What case is this? Danger or no danger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's rule seems wrong whether or not there is danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there is danger, then even wood of an אשירה should be allowed! And if there is no danger, then even all other Torah prohibitions should not be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule by testing both possible cases. Neither one seems to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a life is at stake, פיקוח נפש normally overrides every prohibition, so why exclude אשירה? If no life is at stake, every forbidden item should be off-limits, so why single out אשירה? The exception makes no sense either way.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances?
Danger to life
Prohibitions of the Torah

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say there is danger,
then even wood of an asheira should also be allowed!
And if there is no danger,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כׇּל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה נָמֵי לָא?!
phrases.english: then even all prohibitions in the Torah should also not be allowed!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי נֵימָא דְּאִיכָּא סַכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's exception for עצי אשירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: in danger everything is allowed, and without danger nothing is allowed, so the exception has no place.

steps.title: There is danger, and still idolatrous wood is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case involves danger, and even so עצי אשירה may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is a case of danger, and even so, wood of an אשירה is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן is talking about a life-threatening case. Even then, idolatry wood stays forbidden. The proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיקוח נפש overrides most prohibitions, but עבודה זרה is an exception. A person must give up his life rather than benefit from idolatry. The גמרא now needs a source for this, and the ברייתא in the next step provides it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeping the first option)
And even so

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think פיקוח נפש overrides everything. עבודה זרה (along with גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים) is one of the cases where one must give up his life.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where there is danger,
and even so, wood of an asheira is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma by choosing the case of danger.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting one side of the dilemma and explaining why the exception still holds
steps.terutzMaskana: Danger permits everything except עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks why both 'all your soul' and 'all your might' are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר asks why the פסוק of ואהבת needs both phrases.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: If it says 'with all your soul,' why does it say 'with all your might'? And if it says 'with all your might,' why does it say 'with all your soul'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof with a ברייתא. Here רבי אליעזר only raises the question, and his answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בכל נפשך״ means giving your life, and ״בכל מאדך״ means giving your money. If you must give your life, money is obviously included. If only money were written, giving life would seem not to be required. So each phrase looks unnecessary next to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
With all your soul, meaning even your life
With all your might, meaning all your money
Why was it stated?

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it is stated 'with all your soul,'
why is it stated 'with all your might'?
And if it is stated 'with all your might,'
why is it stated 'with all your soul'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source for the answer in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That one must give up his life rather than benefit from עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר on the פסוק ״ואהבת את ה׳ אלקיך״

steps.title: Each phrase speaks to a different kind of person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that both phrases are needed. Some people value their body more, and some value their money more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is to tell you: If there is a person whose body is dearer to him than his money, for him it says 'with all your soul.' And if there is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body, for him it says 'with all your might.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question. This completes the proof that אהבת ה׳ can require giving up one's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people differ, neither phrase can be learned from the other, so both are written. The key point for our סוגיא is ״בכל נפשך״: a person must give up his life for ה׳, and this applies to עבודה זרה. That is why one may not heal with עצי אשירה even in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, to tell you
Dear to him
His body
His money

steps.whatToRemember: Even when life is in danger, one may not heal with עצי אשירה. ״בכל נפשך״ teaches that one must give up his life rather than serve or benefit from עבודה זרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the rule that עבודה זרה is יהרג ואל יעבור, even when the 'transgression' is only using it for healing.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁגּוּפוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִמָּמוֹנוֹ —
phrases.english: If there is a person whose body is dearer to him than his money,
for this it is stated 'with all your soul.'

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁמָּמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ —
phrases.english: And there is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body,
for this it is stated 'with all your might.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 17 and completes the proof for step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both phrases are needed because people value body and money differently. ״בכל נפשך״ requires giving up one's life for ה׳.

steps.title: רבין's version: healing is allowed except through עבודה זרה or גילוי עריות
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that a person may heal himself with anything, except through עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said that רבי יוחנן said: A person may heal himself with anything, except with עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רבי יוחנן's rule about healing with forbidden things. This report comes from רבין. Its list of exceptions begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14, רבי יעקב quoted רבי יוחנן as saying the only exception is עצי אשירה, which is wood used for idol worship. רבין's version is wider. It forbids healing through anything connected to עבודה זרה, and it adds גילוי עריות. The sentence continues on the next amud with a third exception, שפיכות דמים.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to Bavel). This is a standard way of introducing a teaching brought over from ארץ ישראל.
One may heal oneself with anything, even with forbidden things.
Except for.
Idol worship. Here it means anything connected to idolatry.
Forbidden sexual relationships.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not contradicting himself here. Two different students, רבי יעקב and רבין, are reporting his teaching in two different versions. רבין's version is the broader one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line begins the list of very serious sins that a person may not commit even to save his life. That list later becomes a basic rule in הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came (from Eretz Yisrael), he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: This is a second report of רבי יוחנן's teaching. It is different from רבי יעקב's report in Step 14.

phrases.english: One may heal oneself with anything,
phrases.notes: This includes things a person is normally forbidden to benefit from.

phrases.english: except for idolatry and forbidden sexual relations...
phrases.notes: The list is broader than just עצי אשירה, and it continues on the next amud (with שפיכות דמים).

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא of רבי אליעזר about giving up one's life for God, the גמרא brings רבין's version of רבי יוחנן's rule. It is broader than רבי יעקב's version in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may heal himself with any forbidden thing, except through עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות. The list continues on the next amud with שפיכות דמים.
